extracted.intended_audience: SNAP stakeholders: State SNAP agencies, Federal policymakers, researchers, advocates, and practitioners implementing SNAP work and E&T policies
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results listing of notices, proposed and final rules, and information-collection requests related to 'SNAP work' (work requirements, Employment & Training (E&T), ABAWDs, QC, retailer standards, and related program administration). It aggregates multiple documents that state substantive regulatory and program-administration requirements and study objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: General SNAP Work Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 establishes national eligibility standards including work requirements: individuals ages 16-59 who are able to work must register for work, accept an offer of suitable employment, and satisfy general work requirement conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced in proposed and final rules describing how the general work requirement applies; used as baseline legal standard for who is subject to work requirements and what behaviors (registering, accepting suitable employment) are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: ABAWD Time Limit and Exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and definitions related to able-bodied adults without dependents (ABAWD) time limit including updates to and definitions of exceptions, and adjustment of the number of discretionary exemptions available to State agencies each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemakings clarify procedures for when State agencies must screen for exceptions to the time limit and verification requirements for exceptions; proposed rules add program-purpose language and amend how exceptions are handled and verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Purpose Language (Assisting Low-Income Adults Obtain Employment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Addition to SNAP program purpose language to include assisting low-income adults in obtaining employment and increasing their earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented through rulemakings that incorporate Fiscal Responsibility Act provisions; affects regulatory interpretation and objectives for SNAP and E&T programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening for Homelessness at Application/Recertification
rubrics_metrics.description: State SNAP agencies are required to screen for homelessness at SNAP application and recertification, and SNAP Quality Control (QC) data are used to estimate how many SNAP participants experience homelessness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency asserts SNAP QC data provide the best available estimate of homelessness among SNAP participants; screening is part of eligibility and exception processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP Employment & Training (E&T) Monitoring, Oversight, and Reporting Measures
rubrics_metrics.description: State agencies are required to report outcome data to USDA/FNS; the Department will monitor and assess State agencies' effectiveness of E&T programs and may require improvements as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule implements Agricultural Act of 2014 E&T provisions: requires reporting measures, outcome data, program monitoring, and authority to require program improvements; aims to determine effectiveness in assisting participants to obtain and retain employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staple Food Stocking Standards for SNAP Retailers
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework and minimum number of distinct staple food varieties retailers must carry (increase from three to seven in each of four staple food categories) and requirements on perishable varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule codifies new framework to ensure retailers effectively serve SNAP participants by offering wider variety; analysis highlights concerns for small-format stores (convenience stores) ability to meet new standards and integrity implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP Quality Control (QC) System Requirements (7 CFR Part 275)
rubrics_metrics.description: legal and administrative basis for the SNAP QC system under Section 16 of the Food and Nutrition Act and SNAP regulations at Part 275, Subpart C; forms include FNS-74A and FNS-74B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices regarding information collection, reinstatements, and revisions to QC collections; QC data used for minimodels and payment-accuracy estimation; includes OMB form numbers and burden statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and Verification of Lottery and Gambling Winnings; Resource Verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals/households must self-report substantial lottery or gambling winnings to State SNAP agencies; State agencies must establish cooperative agreements with gaming entities to identify participants with substantial winnings; resource verification at application and recertification is required under specific CFR citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information-collection notices provide burden estimates (cases, hours, costs) and cite CFR sections (e.g., 7 CFR 273.11(r), 7 CFR 273.2(f)(1) & (2)); noncompliance affects eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: National SNAP Information Database Security Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The National SNAP Information Database will utilize technical safeguards to ensure integrity and meet technical safeguards required by its system categorization in NIST 800-53, hosted in a secure environment with perimeter security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy Act/System of Records notice describes security design and purpose (validate eligibility determinations, strengthen program integrity) and expectations for technical safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating the Interview Requirement for SNAP Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Study objectives to describe effects of waiving the interview requirement on agency processes, staff experiences, applicant and recipient outcomes, and lessons for future policy or implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New information collection request; respondent groups include State directors, field managers, eligibility workers, CBOs, and SNAP applicants/participants—study will analyze differences in outcomes and implementation experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing Equity in SNAP Work Requirements and E&T Administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Study to inform FNS about options for assessing and monitoring equity in administration of SNAP work requirements and E&T services, including identifying areas where equity issues could occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives include: (1) identify areas in administration/access where equity issues could occur; (2) identify data to assess access/outcomes; (3) describe how State agencies address equity; (4) develop recommendations for assessing/measuring equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization of State Heating and Cooling Standard Utility Allowances (SUAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires State agencies to submit SUA methodologies for FNS approval at least every five years and to ensure baseline expenditure data and methodology reflect recent trends and changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule intends to ensure consistency and integrity of SUAs across the country; methodologies must demonstrate alignment with low-income household utility cost data and account for changes (e.g., internet treated as allowable shelter expense).

rubrics_metrics.name: E&T Case Management, Notifications, and Data Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement for case management services to individuals participating in SNAP E&T; State agencies must notify individuals deemed ill-suited for an E&T component; State agencies must inform ABAWDs about work requirements and the ABAWD time limit; addition of data elements to FNS-583 SNAP E&T Activity Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information-collection notice explains merging provisions into existing collections, specifies notifications and reporting changes, and outlines who must receive particular communications at recertification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Assessment (RA) Tools for Payment Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of RA tools (statistical models using SNAP household characteristics) by State agencies to estimate relative risk of improper payment; study to provide information about use, effects, and best practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data collection planned via a web-based census of 53 State agencies and case studies with interviews of various state/local staff; results intended to inform FNS and State agencies about RA tool development and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification and Calculation Methods for Compliance with Work Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods PHAs/Owners (in HUD context) would use to verify compliance with work requirements, including options to require fixed hours per week or average hours per week and responsibilities for verification and enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed HUD rule allows flexibility (fixed or average hours) to accommodate variable schedules; PHAs/Owners responsible for verification procedures, including how to calculate averages and document compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for Implementation of Work Requirements and Term Limits in Housing Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule giving PHAs and certain Multifamily Housing Owners discretion to implement work requirements and term limits for work-eligible adults, consistent with statutory goals to promote self-sufficiency and local flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule text outlines policy goals, affected programs (public housing, HCV, PBV, PBRA), verification responsibilities, and options for how work activities/hours may be measured; includes enforcement and documentation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on Use and Disclosure of SNAP Application/Case File Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collected from SNAP application forms or contained in case files may only be used or disclosed to certain persons as specified by statute and regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices on information collection and forms emphasize privacy and limited disclosures consistent with statutory limits; used to ensure correct benefit amounts and eligibility while protecting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SNAP QC Minimodel for Policy Impact Estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: The SNAP QC Minimodel is used by FNS to estimate impacts of policy changes on current SNAP households, relying on QC data that are statistically representative nationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology sections describe data windows used (e.g., Oct 2021–Sept 2022) and that QC data are collected annually; minimodels support measuring transfer changes and estimating policy impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retailer Integrity Risk and Sanctions Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis showing that small-format retailers (convenience stores) account for a high share of SNAP retailer sanctions and represent integrity risk while providing a small share of redemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in rulemaking to justify retailer stocking and participation rules; empirical evidence informs which retailer types pose greater integrity risk and access implications for SNAP households.
